brief:
Gaza's war has shattered longstanding bipartisan support for Israel in Washington, marking a significant shift in American politics after decades of near-universal backing, Al Jazeera English reported. The conflict has prompted rare public criticism from US lawmakers and altered the political landscape in ways that fundamentally challenge Israel's previously protected status.

The investigation examines how the Gaza crisis catalyzed this break with tradition and what the realignment means for US Middle East policy going forward. Shifting congressional dynamics and changing public opinion suggest the unwavering support Israel once commanded faces new constraints and competing pressures within American politics.
dek: For decades, Israel was untouchable in Washington. Gaza changed that. Josh Rushing investigates how and what comes next.
title: Gaza fractures decades-long US political consensus on Israel
